questions.q: In a hydraulic lift, the surface area of the input piston is \(6 $\mathrm{~cm}^2\) and that of the output piston is \(1500 $\mathrm{~cm}^2\). If 100 N force is applied to the input piston to raise the output piston by 20 cm, then the work done is _______ kJ.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{F}_1}{\mathrm{~A}_1}=\frac{\mathrm{F}_2}{\mathrm{~A}_2}, \frac{100}{6}=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{1500}, \mathrm{~F}=\frac{50}{3} \times 1500 \\ & \mathrm{~F}=50 \times 500=25 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~N} \\ & \omega=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}} . \overrightarrow{\mathrm{S}}=25 \times 10^3 \times \frac{20}{100} \\ & =5 \times 10^3=5 \mathrm{~kJ}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The reading of pressure metre attached with a closed pipe is $4 . 5 \times {10}^{4}Nm^{- 2}$. On opening the valve, water starts flowing and the reading of pressure metre falls to $2 . 0 \times {10}^{4}Nm^{- 2}$. The velocity of water is found to be $\sqrt{V}ms^{- 1}$. The value of $V$ is _________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the change in pressure can be written as

${P}_{1} - {P}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}ρv^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$4 . 5 \times {10}^{4} -2 . 0 \times {10}^{4} = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times {10}^{3} \timesv^{2}$⇒ 2 . 5 \times {10}^{4} = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times {10}^{3} \timesv^{2}$⇒ v^{2} = 50 ⇒ v = $\sqrt{50}

Hence, $V = 50.

$

questions.q: There is an air bubble of radius $1 . 0mm$ in a liquid of surface tension $0 . 075Nm^{– 1}$ and density $1000kgm^{– 3}$~at a depth of $10$ cm below the free surface. The amount by which the pressure inside the bubble is greater than the atmospheric pressure is _______ $Pa  \left(g = 10ms^{- 2}\right).$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The pressure inside the bubble is given by&

$\Delta P = P - {P}_{0} = ρgh + \dfrac{2T}{r}$

The data given is~

$r = {10}^{- 3}mT = 0 . 075Nm^{- 1}ρ = 1000kgm^{- 3}h = 10cm$

Therefore, the pressure in the bubble is~

$\Delta P = \left(1000 \times 10 \times 10 \times {10}^{- 2}\right) + \dfrac{2 \times 0 . 075}{10- 3} = 1000 + 150 = 1150Pa$

questions.q: A small spherical ball of radius $0 . 1mm$ and density ${10}^{4}kgm^{- 3}$ falls freely under gravity through a distance $h$ before entering a tank of water. If, after entering the water the velocity of ball does not change and it continue to fall with same constant velocity inside water, then the value of $h$ will be~____ $m$. (Given $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$, viscosity of water $= 1 . 0 \times {10}^{- 5}N ‐ sm^{- 2}$ ).&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using equation of motion,& $v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as$

$v^{2} = 0 + 2 \left(-g\right) \left(-$h\right)$

$⇒ v^{2} = 2gh$

Initial velocity of ball is~$v = $\sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{20h}.

~If after entering the water this velocity does not change, then this value should be equal to the terminal velocity.

Then,~\sqrt{2gh} = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{r^{2}\left(ρ - \sigma\right)g}{η},here,~$ρ$~is density of ball,~\sigma~is density of water and~$η$~is viscosity.

$⇒ $\sqrt{20h} = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{\left(0 . 1 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)2\left({10}^{4} - {10}^{3}\right)10}{1 \times {10}^{- 5}}$⇒ $\sqrt{20h} = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{{10}^{- 8}\left(10 - 1\right){10}^{3} \times 10}{1 \times {10}^{- 5}}

$⇒ 20h = 400$

$∴ h = 20m$

$

questions.q: In a test experiment on a model aeroplane in wind tunnel, the flow speeds on the upper and lower surfaces of the wings are $70ms^{- 1}$ and $65ms^{- 1}$ respectively. If the wing area is $2m^{2}$, the lift of the wing is _______N$. (Given density of air $= 1 . 2kgm^{- 3})
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying Bernoulli's principle on upper & lower surfaces, we get

${P}_{1} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ\left({v}_{1}\right)2 + ρg{h}_{1} = {P}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ\left({v}_{2}\right)2 + ρg{h}_{2}$

Since, height difference between upper and lower surface is negligible.

$⇒ {P}_{2} - {P}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}ρ\left({v}_{1}\right)2 - \dfrac{1}{2}ρ\left({v}_{2}\right)2$

Therefore, upthrust acting due to pressure difference:

$⇒ \dfrac{F}{A} = \dfrac{1}{2}ρ\left({v}_{1}^{2} - {v}_{2}^{2}\right) ⇒ F = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 . 2 \times \left({70}^{2} - {65}^{2}\right) \times 2$

$= 810N$

questions.q: $64$ identical drops each charged upto potential of $10mV$~are combined to form a bigger drop. The potential of the bigger drop will be _____ $mV$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the potential& \left(V\right)$~of each tiny drop is given by

$V = k\dfrac{q}{r} . . . \left(1\right)$

When all the drops forms the bigger drop the radius of the new drop~ \left(r '\right)$~can be calculated as follows:

\begin{cases}$Volumeofbigdrop & = & 64 \timesvolumeofeachtinydrop \\ ⇒ & $\dfrac{4}{3}\pir{'}^{3} =$64 \times $\dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}$\\ ⇒ & r ' = 4r\end{cases}$

So, the potential of the new big drop \left(V '\right)$~can be written as

\begin{cases}$V ' & = & $k\dfrac{64q}{r '}$\\ = & $k\dfrac{64q}{4r}$\\ = & $16k\dfrac{q}{r} . . . \left($2\right)\end{cases}$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and simplify to obtain the potential of the new drop.

\begin{cases}\dfrac{V '}{V}$& = & $\dfrac{16k\dfrac{q}{r}}{k\dfrac{q}{r}}$\\ ⇒ & V ' = 16V . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the value of the known parameter into equation (3) to calculate the required value of the potential for the new drop.

\begin{cases}$V ' & = & 16 \times10mV \\ = & 160mV\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: The diameter of an air bubble which was initially $2$ mm, rises steadily through a solution of density $1750 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ at the rate of $0.35 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$. Coefficient of viscosity of the solution is ______ (Assume mass of the bubble to be negligible) (Answer in Poise to the nearest integer)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As the bubble is rising steadily the net force acting on it will be zero.

(Because of density of air is negligible, so the value of $mg$ can be neglected)

So, the force of buoyancy $B$ is equal to the weight of the displaced liquid acting upward is equal to the viscous force acting downward, i.e.,~$B = F$.

$⇒ \dfrac{4\pi}{3}R^{3}ρg = 6\piηRv$

Putting $R = 1mm = {10}^{- 3}m$,~$ρ = 1 . 75 \times {10}^{3}kgm^{- 3}$,~$g = 10ms^{- 2}$~and~$v = 0 . 35 \times {10}^{- 2}ms^{- 1}$

$η = \dfrac{10}{9} = 1 \cdot 11$

In~SI unit,~$η = 11$~poise \left(CGS\right)$.

$

questions.q: A liquid of density $750kgm^{- 3}$ flows smoothly through a horizontal pipe that tapers in cross-sectional area from ${A}_{1} = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2}m^{2}$ to ${A}_{2} = \dfrac{A1}{2}$. The pressure difference between the wide and narrow sections of the pipe is $4500Pa$. The rate of flow of liquid is _____~$\times {10}^{- 3}m^{3}s^{- 1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the equation of continuity,& ${v}_{2} = 2{v}_{1}$.

Applying the Bernoulli's Theorem,

${P}_{1} + \dfrac{ρ{v1}^{2}}{2} = {P}_{2} + \dfrac{ρ4\left({v}_{1}\right)2}{2}⇒ {P}_{1} - {P}_{2} = \dfrac{3ρ{v1}^{2}}{2}$

$⇒ 4500 = \dfrac{3 \times 750 \times {v1}^{2}}{2} ⇒ {v}_{1} = 2ms^{- 1}$

Now volume flow rate,$Q = A{v}_{1} = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 2 = 24 \times {10}^{- 3}m^{3}s^{- 1}$

questions.q: A metal block of base area $0 . 20m^{2}$ is placed on a table, as shown in figure. A liquid film of thickness $0 . 25mm$ is inserted between the block and the table. The block is pushed by a horizontal force of $0 . 1N$ and moves with a constant speed. If the viscosity of the liquid is $5 . 0 \times {10}^{– 3}Pl$, the speed of block is ______~$\times {10}^{- 3}ms^{- 1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Viscous force is given by,

$| F | = ηA\dfrac{\Deltav}{\Deltah}$

$⇒ 0 . 1 = 5 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 0 . 2 \times \dfrac{v}{0 . 25 \times {10}^{- 3}}$

$⇒ v = 0 . 025ms^{- 1}$

$⇒ v = 25 \times {10}^{- 3}ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A soap bubble of the radius $3$ cm is formed inside another soap bubble of radius,~$6$ cm. The radius of an equivalent soap bubble that has~the same excess pressure as inside the smaller bubble with respect to the atmospheric pressure is____cm .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula of excess pressure inside the soap bubble is,& $\dfrac{4T}{R}$~here~$T$~is the surface tension and~$R$~is the radius of the soap bubble,~

$⇒ {P}_{0} + \dfrac{4T}{6} + \dfrac{4T}{3} = {P}_{0} + \dfrac{4T}{R}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{R}⇒ R = 2cm$.

questions.q: The velocity of upper layer of water in a river is $36kmh^{- 1}$. Shearing stress between horizontal layers of water is ${10}^{- 3}Nm^{- 2}$. Depth of the river is _____~$m$. (Co-efficient of viscosity of water is ${10}^{- 2}Pas$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The viscous force formula is given by,

$F = - ηA\dfrac{d v}{d y}$

Therefore, shear stress~$\dfrac{F}{A} = - η\dfrac{d v}{d y}$. Here negative sign tells us that the direction of force is opposite to the velocity gradient.

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{F}{A}\right| = η\dfrac{d v}{d y}$

Now~$v = 36 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 10ms^{- 1}$~and if the depth is~$d$

$\dfrac{d v}{d y} = \dfrac{10}{d}$

$⇒ {10}^{- 3} = {10}^{- 2} \times \dfrac{10}{d} ⇒ d = 100m$

questions.q: A big drop is formed by coalescing 1000 small droplets of water. The ratio of surface energy of 1000 droplets to that of energy of big drop is $\frac{10}{x}$. The value of $x$ is __________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} 1000 \frac{4}{3} \pi r^3 & =\frac{4}{3} \pi R^3 \\ 10 r & =R \\ R & =10 r\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \frac{\text { S.E. of } 1000 \text { drops }}{\text { S.E. of Big drop }} & =\frac{1000\left(4 \pi \mathrm{r}^2\right) \mathrm{T}}{4 \pi \mathrm{R}^2 \mathrm{~T}} \\ & =\frac{1000 \times \mathrm{r}^2}{(10 \mathrm{r})^2}=10=\frac{10}{\mathrm{x}} \\ \therefore \quad x & =1\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Small water droplets of radius $0.01 \mathrm{~mm}$ are formed in the upper atmosphere and falling with a terminal velocity of $10 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$. Due to condensation, if 8 such droplets are coalesced and formed a larger drop, the new terminal velocity will be _____\mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{s}.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{m}=$ mass of small drop
$\mathrm{M}=$ mass of bigger drop
$\begin{aligned} & V_t=\frac{2}{9} \frac{R^2(\rho-\sigma) g}{\eta} \\ & 8 \propto m=M \\ & 8 r^3=R^3 \Rightarrow R=2 R\end{aligned}$
as $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{t}} \times \mathrm{R}^2 \quad \because$ Radius double so $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{t}}$ becomes 4 time
$\therefore 4 \times 10=40 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$

questions.q: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble A in air is half the excess pressure inside another soap bubble B in air. If the volume of the bubble A is $n$ times the volume of the bubble $B$, then, the value of $n$ is ___.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{P}=\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\Delta \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}}=2 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{B}}}\right)^3=8\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An air bubble of diameter $6$ mm rises steadily through a solution of density $1750kgm^{- 3}$~at the rate of $0 . 35cms^{- 1}$. The co-efficient of viscosity of the solution (neglect density of air) is ________ Pas (given, $g = 10ms^{- 2}$).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The bubble is moving with a constant velocity so the net force acting on the body is zero.

Stokes' law defines the drag force which& is given by& $F = 6\piηrv$

The buoyant force is given by~$B = Vρg = \dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}ρg$

Hence, it can be written that

$\dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}ρg = 6\piηrv ⇒ η = \dfrac{2r^{2}ρg}{9v} = \dfrac{2 \times \left(3 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)2 \times 1750 \times 10}{9 \times 0 . 35 \times {10}^{- 2}} = 10Pas$&

questions.q: $A soap bubble is blown to a diameter of $7 \mathrm{~cm} .36960 \mathrm{erg}$ of work is done in blowing it further. If surface tension of soap solution is $40 \mathrm{dyne} / \mathrm{cm}$ then the new radius is______ $\mathrm{cm}$ Take  \left(\pi=\frac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \omega=\Delta \mathrm{U}=\mathrm{S} \Delta \mathrm{A} \\ & 36960 \mathrm{erg}=\frac{40 \text { dyne }}{\mathrm{cm}} 8 \pi\left[(\mathrm{r})^2-\left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^2\right] \mathrm{cm}^2 \\ & \mathrm{r}=7 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Suppose you have taken a dilute solution of oleic acid in such a way that its concentration becomes $0 . 01{cm}^{3}$ of oleic acid per ${cm}^{3}$ of the solution. Then you make a thin film of this solution (monomolecular thickness) of area $4{cm}^{2}$ by considering $100$ spherical drops of radius \left(\dfrac{3}{40\pi}\right)\dfrac{1}{3} \times {10}^{- 3}cm .$ Then the thickness of oleic acid layer will be $x \times {10}^{- 14}m$. Where $x$ is ________ .$
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: A spherical drop of liquid splits into $1000$ identical spherical drops. If ${u}_{i}$ is the surface energy of the original drop and ${u}_{f}$ is the total surface energy of the resulting drops, the (ignoring evaporation),~$\dfrac{uf}{ui} = \left(\dfrac{10}{x}\right).~Then value of $x$ is \text{ and } ______:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let& $R$~be the~radius of bigger drop and~$r$~be the radius of smaller drop.

Here, volume will remain conserved, so~${V}_{R} = {V}_{r}$.

$⇒ \dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3} = 1000 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}$

$⇒ R = 10r$

As surface energy is stated as~$u = SA$, here,~$S$~is surface tension and~$A$~is~surface area.

Thus,~${u}_{i} = S \left(4\piR^{2}\right)$~and~${u}_{f} = S\left(4\pir^{2}\right) \times1000$

The ratio is~\dfrac{uf}{ui} = \dfrac{1000r^{2}}{R2}

$⇒ $\dfrac{uf}{ui} = \dfrac{10}{1}

Hence, the value of~$x = 1.

$

questions.q: An air bubble of radius 1.0 mm is observed at a depth of 20 cm below the free surface of a liquid having surface tension $0.095 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{m}^2$ and density $10^3 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$. The difference between pressure inside the bubble and atmospheric pressure is _____ $\mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m}^2$. (Take $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\Delta \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{in}}-\mathrm{P}_0\begin{aligned} & =\rho \mathrm{gh}+\frac{2 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}}=\frac{1000 \times 10 \times 20}{100}+\frac{2 \times 0.095}{10^{-3}} \\ & =2000+190 \\ & =2190\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The surface tension of soap solution is & $3 . 5 \times {10}^{- 2}Nm^{- 1}$. The amount of work done required to increase the radius of soap bubble from $10$ cm to $20$ cm is _____\times {10}^{- 4}J$~. (take $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7})
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The amount of work done is equal to the change in the surface energy to increase the radius of the bubble.

The formula to calculate the change in surface energy is given by

& $\Delta U = 2 ( T \times \Delta A ) . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required work done.

\begin{cases}$∆ U & = & 3 . 5 \times {10}^{- 2} \ttimes4\pi \left[(0 . 2{)}^{2} - ( 0 . 1{)}^{2}\right]\times2J \\ = & 3 . 5 \times {10}^{- 2} \times4 \times $\dfrac{22}{7} \times$0 . 03 \times2 \\ = & 2 \times1 . 32 \times {10}^{- 2}\\ = & 264 \times {10}^{- 4}J\end{cases}

$
